claims.text: A medium air/fuel-pressure setting on a low-temperature ID-HVAF i7 torch with propylene fuel can produce an approximately 150 μm FeCoNiCrAl bond coat.
The proposed process will preserve low porosity and minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The proposed feedstock has a particle-size range of 5–30 μm.
The feedstock contains Al-rich and Cr-rich microsegregated regions.
The initial FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a BCC random-solid-solution structure.
The Inconel 718 substrates have a grit-blasted roughness of Ra 3.9 ± 0.6 μm.
A 63 mm 3L4 nozzle and 2.75 mm powder injector operated at medium air/fuel pressure provide the best deposition performance.
The medium-pressure process will produce a coating with approximately 0.2% porosity.
The deposited coating will have a uniform elemental distribution and retain the BCC random-solid-solution structure.
Oxidation will produce an approximately 3 μm interdiffusion zone and a thin, continuous, predominantly Al2O3 thermally grown oxide.
Low-temperature HVAF-i7 processing minimizes deposition-stage oxidation.
Low coating porosity restricts oxygen ingress and internal oxidation.
Controlled outward diffusion of Al forms a protective, thin alumina scale during high-temperature exposure.
Sluggish diffusion inherent to the HEA structure limits oxide growth and mixed-oxide formation.
Low- and high-pressure baseline coatings have porosities of 0.8% and 1.8%, respectively.
Low- and high-pressure baseline coatings have deposition efficiencies of 73% and 53%, respectively.
Feedstock in the 15–45 μm range was inadequate for producing the required coating thickness.
The proposed coating will retain a thin, predominantly Al2O3 TGO and preserve integrity during isothermal air exposures at 1000–1150 °C for up to 50 hours.
Longer or hotter exposures may cause spallation because the alloy lacks reactive elements such as Y or Hf.

contradictions.description: The baseline shortfall is attributed to 15–45 μm feedstock, but the proposed initial state uses 5–30 μm feedstock while the stated intervention focuses on pressure/nozzle configuration and target thickness. This introduces an unacknowledged feedstock-size change, so the proposal is not a clean single-intervention comparison.

The requested comparison is relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, but the predicted outcome is framed mainly against low- and high-pressure coatings. The baseline and experimental comparator are therefore not consistently defined.
